enemies.name: Awakened One
enemies.description: The Awakened One is a boss in Act III that punishes players for over-relying on Power cards. It fights in two phases: in the first (Unawakened) phase it builds strength based on your use of Powers, then when defeated it kills debuffs, rebirths, and transitions into an Awakened form with stronger attacks. The fight tests both your defense and timing—knowing when to use powers vs when to hold back is key.

enemies.name: Bronze Automaton
enemies.description: Bronze Automaton is one of the three possible Act II bosses in *Slay the Spire*. This mechanical foe showcases both raw power and disruption, spawning Bronze Orbs which steal cards and forcing you to balance offense with control. Its Hyper Beam attack can punish unprepared decks, making this fight a test of deck efficiency, timing, and resilience.

enemies.name: Donu and Deca
enemies.description: Donu & Deca are the Act III boss duo who force you to handle simultaneous threats. Donu boosts strength for both itself and Deca every other turn, while Deca provides defensive support and adds Dazed cards. Their pattern is consistent, but their combined output becomes dangerous quickly. Deciding whether to kill Donu first (to stop strength scaling) or Deca first (to stop Dazed spam and big blockers) often determines the outcome.

enemies.name: Guardian
enemies.description: The Guardian is one of the three possible Act 1 bosses in Slay the Spire, a towering mechanical construct designed to defend the Spire’s secrets. Known for its deadly multi-hit attacks and powerful defensive stance, the Guardian alternates between offense and defense, forcing players to carefully manage their timing and resources. Its signature mechanic is the Mode Shift, which activates after taking a set amount of damage, causing the Guardian to curl into a defensive ball that reduces incoming damage and unleashes counterattacks. With the ability to punish reckless play and overwhelm unprepared decks, the Guardian is a true test of block management, burst damage, and deck consistency early in the game. Defeating it rewards players with a powerful Boss Relic and progression into Act 2.

enemies.name: Hexaghost
enemies.description: Hexaghost is an Act I boss whose danger grows with time. It starts with special setup moves, then cycles through attacks that build up flame tokens; once it has accumulated six flames, it unleashes a powerful Inferno attack. Damage from its Divider move also scales with your current HP, making the fight harder if you go in too healthy. Speed and managing burn/status effects are critical for victory.

enemies.name: Slime Boss
enemies.description: The Slime Boss is one of the three possible Act 1 bosses in Slay the Spire, serving as a major early-game challenge for all characters. This massive, gelatinous foe is known for its devastating Slam attack, which can deal huge damage if left unchecked. Unique to the Slime Boss is its ability to Split—once reduced to half health, it divides into two medium Slimes, each capable of summoning additional Spike Slimes or using debuff attacks to weaken the player. Success against the Slime Boss requires smart damage management, careful deck building, and knowing when to push for a split to avoid taking lethal blows. Defeating this boss marks a significant milestone, granting powerful Relics and paving the way into Act 2 of the Spire.

enemies.name: The Champ
enemies.description: The Champ is an Act II boss whose danger escalates as the fight progresses. It features two phases: before and after dropping below half health. Early on it uses debuffs, vulnerable/weak, and moderate damage; once enraged in Phase 2, hits become much more threatening. Beating The Champ requires you to survive early tempo swings and burst through its second phase before you’re overwhelmed.

enemies.name: The Collector
enemies.description: The Collector is an Act II boss known for its minions (Torch Heads), heavy debuffing, and balancing act between dealing with adds and the boss itself. It can apply multiple Weak, Vulnerable, and Frail through its Mega Debuff, and buff both itself and its minions, forcing the player to decide whether to focus on control, crowd‑clear, or burst damage.

enemies.name: The Corrupt Heart
enemies.description: The Corrupt Heart is the final boss in *Slay the Spire*, encountered in Act IV. It tests virtually every mechanic you’ve built up: large HP, damage caps, status effects, and scaling buffs. To beat it, you’ll need strong defense, ways to manage or disable its strengths (like Invincible), and careful planning of your turns to survive both status and attack bursts.

enemies.name: Time Eater
enemies.description: The Time Eater is an Act III boss that punishes decks that play too many cards per turn. It ramps its threat using Time Warp, which tracks how many cards you play; once you hit certain thresholds it can force your turn end and buff itself. It also has a Haste move once its health drops below half, making it very dangerous if you don’t plan burst damage around that phase shift.

enemies.name: Book of Stabbing
enemies.description: The Book of Stabbing is an Act II elite that specializes in scaling multi‑hit attacks, combined with the threat of shuffling Wound cards into your discard pile when you take unblocked damage. It becomes more dangerous over time (especially if not dealt with quickly) because its multi‑stab attack increases in strength with each use.

enemies.name: Giant Head
enemies.description: Giant Head is an Act III elite with very high HP and a scaling attack pattern. It starts with debuffs or weaker attacks (Count or Glare) and after its countdown ends, switches to its powerful ‘It Is Time’ move, which deals heavy damage that increases each time it’s used. Decks that draw many cards or deal high single‑target damage have advantage here.

enemies.name: Gremlin Leader
enemies.description: Gremlin Leader is an Act II elite who commands Gremlin minions. She buffs Strength, grants block to her minions, and summons others via Rally. The threat arises both from her attacks and from the Gremlins she spawns. Removing minions or heavy AoE helps neutralize her advantage quickly.

enemies.name: Gremlin Nob
enemies.description: The Gremlin Nob is an Act I elite in *Slay the Spire* who becomes increasingly dangerous as the fight goes on. It applies the Enrage buff to itself whenever you play Skills, and uses attacks that can also apply Vulnerable. Between the strength growth and debuff pressure, it punishes slow, defensive strategies heavily.

enemies.name: Lagavulin
enemies.description: Lagavulin is an Act I elite, initially passive (Asleep) for its first three turns, giving players time to prepare. Once awakened, it loses its Metallicize buff and begins repeating a pattern of two high‑damage attacks followed by a powerful debuff that weakens your Dexterity and Strength. It’s a fight that rewards setting up early, then pushing hard once it becomes active.

enemies.name: Nemesis
enemies.description: Nemesis is an Act III elite known for alternating Intangible turns, which force you to time your attacks carefully, and for adding Burns to your deck (or applying status effects). It has three possible moves (a triple‑attack, a triple burn move, and a scythe attack) and cannot repeat some moves twice in succession. Managing when to hit vs when to block or buff is critical here.

enemies.name: Reptomancer
enemies.description: Reptomancer is an Act III elite who summons Daggers that threaten to overwhelm you if left unchecked. She starts combat by summoning, then alternates between heavy strikes and summoning based on how many Daggers are on the field. Good AoE, fast removal, and managing status are essential to survive her pressure.

enemies.name: Spire Shield
enemies.description: Spire Shield is one half of the Act IV elite duo (with Spire Spear). It’s the more defensive side: moderate HP, block generation, and abilities that can debuff the player's Strength/Focus if certain conditions are met. Facing Shield forces you to manage orientation (back vs front) and make tough choices about who to attack first.

enemies.name: Spire Spear
enemies.description: Spire Spear is the offensive half of the Act IV elite pair with Spire Shield. It has more HP, focuses on damage and debuffing (Burn insertion, Strength buffs), and its multi‑hit attacks become very dangerous, especially when Shield is boosting its defenses at the same time.

enemies.name: Taskmaster
enemies.description: Taskmaster is an Act II elite who fights alongside two Slavers (Red and Blue). He specializes in shuffling Wounds into your discard pile and dealing moderate damage, making slow decks suffer heavily. Keeping up pressure and choosing which enemy to eliminate first (especially the Red Slaver) often decides the battle.

enemies.name: Three Sentries
enemies.description: A group elite encounter in Act I composed of three Sentry monsters. They combine moderate attacks with status flooding (Dazed cards) and force you to deal with multiple threats simultaneously. The fight emphasizes managing the board, handling status, and targeting priorities carefully.

enemies.name: Acid Slime (L)
enemies.description: A large acid slime in Act I that uses corrosive attacks and will split into two medium acid slimes once reduced to 50% HP. Balancing damage and avoiding status effects is key to managing the split effectively.

enemies.name: Acid Slime (M)
enemies.description: A medium acid slime in Act I. Has same moves as the large slime except it cannot split. Easier to handle but still dangerous with status infliction and moderate damage.

enemies.name: Acid Slime (S)
enemies.description: A small acid slime in Act I. Low HP and weak damage, but its status infliction makes it dangerous in numbers. Alternates between two moves, often Lick and Tackle.

enemies.name: Blue Slaver
enemies.description: A mid‑tier monster in Act I, Blue Slaver alternates between strong attacks and applying Weak. While its base damage isn’t huge, its ability to inflict Weak and inability to repeat the same move too many times means you need to adapt quickly or get worn down over time.

enemies.name: Byrd
enemies.description: Byrds are Act II monsters who begin each battle with a Flying buff, which makes them take only half damage until they are hit a certain number of times in a single turn. They deal modest damage but can become much more dangerous if you let them build up Image Strength. Fighting them well means balancing multi‑hit attacks, status effects, and good timing to force their Flying buff to fall.

enemies.name: Centurion
enemies.description: The Centurion is an Act II monster who fights alongside the Mystic. Its moves include alternating between strong single attacks or defending depending on whether the Mystic is alive. If the Mystic is defeated, the Centurion shifts into a more aggressive form, replacing its defend move with a multi‑hit Fury. Strategic targeting (deciding whether to kill Mystic first) is its major decision point.

enemies.name: Chosen
enemies.description: The Chosen is an Act II monster that alternates between powerful attacks, debuffs, and a Hex power which punishes you for playing non‑Attack cards by adding Dazed to your draw pile. Its pattern and fairly high HP make it a dangerous foe if not handled quickly and precisely.

enemies.name: Cultist
enemies.description: The Cultist is a recurring enemy in *Slay the Spire* that appears in Acts I, II, and III. It starts combat by buffing itself with the Ritual power to gain Strength each turn, then alternates with attacking via Dark Strike. Though its initial damage is modest, the strength gain makes it more threatening over time, especially in longer fights or when paired with other enemies.

enemies.name: Darkling
enemies.description: Darklings are Act III enemies that fight in groups of three. They begin combat with the Life Link buff, meaning that when one dies its body lingers and can be revived if its allies are still alive. Their move set includes Nip, Chomp, and Harden, making them a mix of damage, block, and threat over time. The fight pressures you to manage multiple enemies and prevent revivals or punishing damage combos.

enemies.name: Exploder
enemies.description: Exploder is a Shape that threatens massive burst damage if left alive. It uses Slam twice, then uses its Explode move, which deals heavy damage when it dies after the timer ends. Managing its timing is key.

enemies.name: Fat Gremlin
enemies.description: The Fat Gremlin appears in groups and applies Weak with its attacks. Its damage can quickly become problematic in large numbers.

enemies.name: Fungi Beast
enemies.description: Fungi Beast is a monster found mainly in Act I (and sometimes Act II alongside Shelled Parasite) that mixes offense with self‑buffing. With its Bite attack and Grow move, it rewards either fast aggression or strong defense depending on your deck. Its death effect, Spore Cloud, can apply Vulnerable to you, so finishing it off decisively is often advantageous.

enemies.name: Green Louse
enemies.description: Green Louse is similar to Red Louse but instead of growing, it mixes in a Web‑Spitting move that applies Weak. It still uses Bite, and has the Curl Up defensive power. In groups, its Weak ability makes them more dangerous by lengthening turns where you must defend.

enemies.name: Gremlin Wizard
enemies.description: The Gremlin Wizard charges for several turns before unleashing a powerful blast. Interrupting it before this happens is crucial.

enemies.name: Jaw Worm
enemies.description: A medium threat in Act I; Jaw Worm balances between offense and defense. It can Chomp, Thrash (attack + block), or Bellow (buff itself & gain Block). In Act III, Jaw Worms sometimes start with the Bellow bonus, making them tougher from the first turn.

enemies.name: Looter
enemies.description: The Looter is an Act II monster with the Thievery power: every time it attacks, it steals a set amount of the player’s gold. If the Looter is killed, the stolen gold is returned. Its moves include Mug (standard attack), Lunge (strong, single hit), Smoke Bomb (block), and Escape (leaves combat, keeping stolen gold). This enemy punishes taking too much damage and neglecting gold economy early on.

enemies.name: Mad Gremlin
enemies.description: The Mad Gremlin grows stronger when attacked due to its Angry power, making it a high priority threat in groups.

enemies.name: Mystic
enemies.description: Mystic is the support half of the Centurion & Mystic combo in Act II. It primarily heals both itself and the Centurion, buffs enemy Strength, and occasionally attacks. Healing is triggered when any enemy can still be healed significantly, so opponents must plan to counter that via burst damage or prevent the healing cycle from becoming overwhelming.

enemies.name: Orb Walker
enemies.description: The Orb Walker is a solo Act III enemy known for snowballing strength over time. It alternates between using a beam attack that shuffles Burns into your deck and a heavy Claw strike. If not killed quickly, its passive Strength gain can overwhelm unprepared players.

enemies.name: Red Louse
enemies.description: One of the weakest Act I enemies; Red Louse alternates between biting and growing stronger. Though low HP, its Strength buffs can make it more dangerous than its damage suggests, especially in groups.

enemies.name: Red Slaver
enemies.description: A more threatening Slaver in Act I, Red Slaver deals damage, applies Vulnerable, and can sometimes Entangle you (preventing Attack cards). Its early threat is higher than Blue Slaver due to debuffs, so managing Vulnerable and avoiding being locked out of attacks should be priorities.

enemies.name: Repulsor
enemies.description: Another Shape from Act III: the Repulsor shuffles Dazed cards into your draw pile via its Repulse move, and it has a Bash option. It’s less about raw damage and more about clogging your deck and controlling tempo.

enemies.name: Shelled Parasite
enemies.description: Shelled Parasite is an Act II monster that is very defensive with its Plated Armor buff. Its moves include life‑steal attacks and heavy single attacks that also apply Image Frail. It has a probabilistic move pattern that makes it somewhat unpredictable, and its Plated Armor makes it resilient to slow damage, so breaking through shields quickly is key. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

enemies.name: Shield Gremlin
enemies.description: Shield Gremlin protects its allies with block. Eliminating it early can prevent longer fights.

enemies.name: Snake Plant
enemies.description: The Snake Plant is an Act II monster with the Malleable power: when it receives attack damage, it gains growing block (Image Block) that increases with each time it's hit in a turn. It mixes multi‑hit attacks and status debuffs (Weak, Frail) via its Enfeebling Spores move. It’s predictable but dangerous because its Malleable block can stack heavily if you use many small attacks or multiple hits in a turn.

enemies.name: Sneaky Gremlin
enemies.description: Sneaky Gremlin deals the highest direct damage among the Gremlins. Its attacks can quickly stack up.

enemies.name: Snecko
enemies.description: Snecko is an Act II monster who introduces randomization mechanics via Confused and Image Vulnerable. It begins with a Confusing gaze, then alternates between bite attacks and a vulnerability‑applying move. Its pattern is semi‑predictable but its status effects can disrupt certain decks dramatically, especially those relying on low‑cost or predictable costs.

enemies.name: Spheric Guardian
enemies.description: Spheric Guardian is an Act II/III monster with very low HP but strong defensive buffs. It starts with Barricade and multiple Artifact charges, meaning its Block persists each turn and status effects are hard to apply. It cycles between attacking and building more Icon Block, making it a tanky wall that often needs strategic removal rather than brute forcing through defense.

enemies.name: Spike Slime (L)
enemies.description: A large spike slime in Act I that shuffles slimed status and inflicts Frail. It also splits into two medium spike slimes when reduced to 50% HP. Moves include Flame Tackle and Lick, with pattern rules preventing long repeats.

enemies.name: Spike Slime (M)
enemies.description: A medium spike slime in Act I. Shares large variant’s offensive moves but no split. Can still inflict status via Lick and uses Flame Tackle to apply Slimed cards.

enemies.name: Spike Slime (S)
enemies.description: A small spike slime in Act I. Straightforward attacker with one simple damage move; weaker but dangerous in groups or paired with slimes that inflict status.

enemies.name: Spiker
enemies.description: A member of the Shapes group in Act III. The Spiker has Image Thorns and alternates between a cutting attack and gaining more Thorns, making it a steady threat especially in prolonged fights.

enemies.name: Spire Growth
enemies.description: Spire Growth is an Act II Elite enemy with high HP and a mix of strong attacks and debilitating debuffs. It is notable for applying Entangled, which prevents the player from playing Attack cards for one turn. Its attack pattern mixes in single heavy hits and multi-hit combos, making it dangerous without consistent Block.

enemies.name: The Maw
enemies.description: The Maw is a large Act III monster with high HP and scaling by buffing itself. It starts fights applying debuffs (Weak & Frail), then alternates between buffing strength, dealing heavy attacks, or consuming players (Nom). Over time its attacks become much worse, especially if it’s not pressured early.

enemies.name: Transient
enemies.description: The Transient is a unique Act III hallway encounter with 999 HP that disappears after 5 turns due to Fading. It only uses one move: a scaling single attack that grows stronger each turn. Because of the Shifting power, it temporarily loses Strength equal to HP lost until the end of each turn. Killing it before it fades awards the achievement 'The Transient'.

enemies.name: Writhing Mass
enemies.description: Writhing Mass is a unique Act III hallway enemy notable for its unpredictable behavior and its ability to end combat prematurely if you cannot manage its HP carefully. It uses a wide range of intents (attacks, blocks, buffs, debuffs) and has a special mechanic: when its HP drops below certain thresholds, it immediately ends the fight and gives only partial rewards unless it is killed outright.
